heading: INT. VILLAGE HALL - FUNERAL RECEPTION - DAY

units.text: INT. VILLAGE HALL - FUNERAL RECEPTION - DAY

Orsolya, 60s, in a black coat stitched with tiny silver thread that moves when nobody is looking, stands by the tea urn while the mourners murmur and the rain taps the leaded windows and a dog under the buffet table sighs, and across the room Bram, 30s, the dead man's nephew, holds a paper plate of untouched sandwiches and watches the coffin lid through the open vestry door as though it might speak.
THE CHOIR gathers by the piano, six old women in grey, humming a note that is slightly too low for the room.

You haven't asked me why I came. Everyone else has. They ask it with their eyebrows. Your uncle owed me a debt, Bram, and in my family we collect, even from the dead. Especially from the dead, who are very bad at hiding.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: He owed everyone. He owed the butcher. It's a funeral, not an audit.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: He owed me his shadow.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: The urn hisses.
The humming from the choir climbs a half step.
That's not funny.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: It wasn't meant to be. Look at the floor beneath the coffin. Go on. The vicar has shuffled four times and still it hasn't moved with him.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: Bram looks.
A dark shape lies against the vestry tiles, long and patient, pointing the wrong way from the candles.
That's the light from the door.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: Is it?
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: Amen.
units.name: THE CHOIR

units.text: Bram? Bram, love, are you in there? Your aunt wants the car brought round.
units.name: A VOICE

units.text: In a minute, Mrs. Pell!
units.name: BRAM

units.text: Do not answer him when he speaks. That is the only rule I will give you. He will use your voice, because it is the nearest one, and he will use your mother's after that.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: Speak. Who speaks?
units.name: BRAM

units.text: The vestry candles bend flat, all together, as if a door had opened onto a great cold field.
The choir stops humming.
The dog under the table stands up, hackles raised, and does not make a sound.
Bram. It's all right. Come and help me with this lid.
units.name: A VOICE

units.text: That is the first.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: How do I stop it?
units.name: BRAM

units.text: You give it what it is owed. And you do not flinch, boy, whatever it wears.
units.name: ORSOLYA

units.text: The shadow on the tiles lifts one edge, slowly, like a hand testing a curtain.
